_contract: Canon secrets registry (CONTENT DEPTH pass, 2026-09-13). This is the source of truth for every secret in the game; scenes/secrets/*.tscn and scenes/props/secret.tscn instances are wired FROM it by the CODE agent. Ids are globally unique: secret_<district>_<NN>. `act` is DERIVED from `district` (GDD 12.3: I=D1-3, II=D4-8, III=D9-11) and must never be assigned independently. `zone` must be an id in that district's content/districts/<district>/item_spawns.json `zones`. `reward.item` must exist in data/items/*.tres. `world_refs` obey the README reachability rule: only ids whose reveal.district is this district or lies in its guaranteed powered_by closure. `en` is the i18n source; key pattern SECRET_<DISTRICT>_<NN>_TITLE/_TEXT. Secrets never restate mechanics and never pre-empt an act gate: an Act I secret hints at the draw, it never names the Architect.
_why_this_file: Before this pass the secret framework was fully plumbed but empty: scripts/world/secret.gd, EventBus.secret_found, three SECRET quests (q_secrets_1..3), achievements secret_hunter + secrets_10, rewards_manager REWARD_SECRET, progress_tracker's persisted `secrets` counter and endings.gd's `secrets >= 3` gate on the Truth ending were all live, yet no secret_id was set anywhere, scenes/props/secret.tscn was instanced by no district, and all 12 scenes/secrets/secret_room_*.tscn were bare Node3D stubs with zero repo-wide references. Net effect: the whole chain was unreachable and the Truth ending could never fire. This registry supplies the missing canon.

_threads.keeper_past: Who the Keeper was before the blackout: forty years of work orders, a family, a ledger, and the moment keeping the light became taking it apart.
_threads.architect_motive: Why Project Architect was built. Never a moustache: a man who believed the city could be taught to remember, and metered what it remembered.
_threads.center_fall: The timeline of the center's fall — night zero, the evacuation, the arena, the nine who came back as something else, and what is still down there.
_threads.grid_crew: Marat, the recorder, the bench proof. The people who kept working the line after the official response stopped answering.

en.title: The Height Mark on the Pole
en.text: Behind the third maple, at knee height, a ladder hook has been bolted to the pole and unbolted again so many times the paint is a white scar. Pencil marks climb the wood beside it, one per year, the last forty crowded together and running out of pole. Someone measured himself against this street every spring. The final mark is fresh, and it is lower than the one before it.

secrets.location_hint: Base of the third lamp pole on the maple row (z_maple_row), behind the trunk, knee height.

en.title: A Lockbox That Was Never Logged Out
en.text: Padlock cut, not picked, and the hasp bent outward: whoever opened this was in a hurry and had a bolt cutter and no intention of coming back. Inside, dry and perfect — two fuses, a length of cable, and a City Power tag with a feeder number nobody issued. In pencil on the inside lid: M. will walk it. Tell him the bench is proof enough.

secrets.location_hint: Padlocked wall lockbox above the workbench in the far garage (z_garage_row).

en.title: The Tin Under the Floorboard
en.text: Second board from the door in the ground-floor hallway, loose at one end, the way a board gets when it is lifted weekly for thirty years. Beneath it: a biscuit tin, a roll of banknotes too old to spend, a wedding ring, and a folded work order in a stranger's handwriting. It reads: LAMP 219, HOUSE 24 — reported out by the occupant, attended same evening, no charge. At the bottom, in a second hand: I will come as long as there is a street to come to.

secrets.location_hint: Loose floorboard in the ground-floor hallway of house 24 (z_house24).

en.title: The Meter That Ran Backwards
en.text: Every meter in this block spins down since the blackout. This one spins up. The housing has been opened and closed by someone who knew how: four screws, no stripped heads, gasket replaced. Inside, the dial has been recalibrated by hand and the new scale is not kilowatt-hours. It is labelled in hours. Somebody is billing this building for time, and the balance is going the wrong way.

secrets.location_hint: Meter cupboard in the boiler room (z_boiler_room), second meter from the left.

en.title: The Keeper's Own Lamp, Still Warm
en.text: Under the workbench in the shed, wrapped in a coat: a service lamp, older than the shed, its glass hand-ground thin so it throws further. The burner is clean. The oil is fresh. On the base, stamped by the utility and then restamped by someone with a smaller punch, so the second mark sits over the first: PROPERTY OF THE CITY, and beneath it, PROPERTY OF NOBODY YET. He has been carrying this one out with him. He means to keep carrying it out.

secrets.location_hint: Under the workbench in the keeper's shed (z_keeper_shed), wrapped in a coat.

en.title: Forty Years of Unfinished Games
en.text: The stone tables in the chess grove each hold a game. None of them are finished. The pieces are set with real care — openings, not nonsense — and every board has been dusted recently, in a city where nobody dusts. Under the north table, taped to the underside, a roll of coins and a note: he always left before I could pay him. Keeping score the only way he'd allow. Tell him I'm even.

secrets.location_hint: Underside of the northernmost chess table in the grove (z_chess_grove).

en.title: What He Threw in the Pond
en.text: The pond is a metre lower than the waterline stain on the stones, and the exposed mud is studded with lamp glass. Not broken — dismantled. Refractors, gaskets, a whole bracket assembly, all laid out by hand and then walked into the water. A man put his own life's work at the bottom of this pond one piece at a time, because a lit lamp is a mouth and he decided to close every mouth he could reach. At the edge, one last bracket, dry, set down neatly. He ran out of pond before he ran out of lamps.

secrets.location_hint: Exposed mud at the drained east edge of the pond (z_pond), among the lamp glass.

en.title: The Shelter Roster Nobody Collected
en.text: The basement shelter holds ninety cots' worth of chalk marks and a clipboard still hanging by the door. Ninety names, ninety tick boxes, eleven ticks. Below the list, in a teacher's careful hand: the buses came at four and took them to the arena. The arena had light. That was the whole of the argument and it won. At the bottom of the page, added later, the pen having gone through the paper: eleven is what came back to be counted. I have stopped writing the other number.

secrets.location_hint: Clipboard hanging inside the basement shelter door (z_basement_shelter).

en.title: The Sub-Feed That Wasn't on the Plan
en.text: Behind the boiler, a conduit runs off the building's own supply and does not appear on the framed electrical plan by the door. The plan is original; the conduit is newer than the paint. It leaves through the north wall toward the park line and it is labelled, in utility stencilling, with a programme name and no department. Whatever they built, they gave it a school's basement to drink from, and they did not tell the caretaker. He knew anyway. The boiler log ends with one line that is not about heat.

secrets.location_hint: Unplanned conduit behind the boiler (z_boiler_room), north wall; the caretaker's log sits on the pipe shelf.

en.title: The Consent Forms, All Signed
en.text: A locked drawer in records, and inside it not one refusal. Two hundred and six consent forms for a study with no control group, every signature present, every date within the same fortnight. The printed heading explains it plainly and horribly: participants will not be informed of the outcome, as the outcome is the point. At the back, a single sheet in the author's own hand, unsigned because he knew it would be read: they volunteered because the lamps were warm and I told them warmth was the treatment. I was not lying. That is the part I cannot put down.

secrets.location_hint: Locked bottom drawer of the records cabinet (z_records), behind the index trays.

en.title: Drawer Nine, Opened From the Inside
en.text: The morgue is cold, has been cold, and nine of its drawers stand open with the catches undamaged. Drawer nine is bent outward at the lip, the steel folded like foil, and the hinge pins are still in their holes. Whatever left did not break out. It decided to leave and the drawer agreed. On the tag, a name, an admission time on night three, and then, in the attendant's shaking capitals: WALKED. NOT DECEASED. NOT DISCHARGED. WALKED. THEY ALL WALKED AND THEY WENT DOWN.

secrets.location_hint: Drawer nine in the morgue wall (z_morgue); the tag hangs from the bent lip.

en.title: The Denial, Corrected by Hand
en.text: Pinned inside the generator room door is the clipping where the director calls Project Architect a maintenance formality and asks the press to move on. Somebody has annotated it in red pencil over months. Beside 'formality': 206 forms. Beside 'no dedicated circuit': sub-feed four, hospital to park. Beside the director's own photograph, a bracket and three words, underlined twice: he signed it too. The last annotation is dated after the blackout and is not in the same hand. It says: he is still signing.

secrets.location_hint: Clipping pinned inside the generator room door (z_generator_room), annotated in red pencil.

en.title: The Tanker That Was Never a Tanker
en.text: The bowser by the pumps has no fuel in it and never had — the filler is welded shut and the tank sounds hollow the wrong way, the way a tank sounds when it is full of something that isn't sloshing. The manifest stapled to the cab lists a cargo of cable, fuses and lamps, and a destination: the center. The crew used a fuel truck to move a grid's worth of light into a place with no road, and they did it often enough to wear the tyres smooth. On the door, stencilled over the company logo: WE STILL DELIVER.

secrets.location_hint: Welded-shut bowser on the forecourt edge (z_tanker); manifest stapled inside the cab door.

en.title: The Scavengers' Rule, Written on the Pump
en.text: The camp behind the shop has been abandoned in a hurry but not in a panic: tins stacked, bedrolls folded, water capped. On the pump island, scratched deep into the paint where everyone would read it, a list of rules. Take the food. Take the fuel. Take the batteries. Then, separately, in bigger letters: DO NOT TAKE THE LAMPS. An old man comes for the lamps. He is not a threat. He will trade. Below it, a tally of trades, kept honestly, and one final line added by a different hand: he asked about the center and we said we didn't know and he looked at us like we were the ones who were lost.

secrets.location_hint: Scratched into the paint of the pump island's outer panel (z_scavenger_camp).

en.title: The Case They Closed by Losing
en.text: Evidence shelf four, one box, one item: a service lamp bracket, catalogued, bagged, tagged with an incident number and no incident behind it. The card says property damage, lamppost, maple row, suspect unknown. The card's been amended three times. First: suspect seen carrying. Second: suspect is removing them, not stealing. Third, and the handwriting stops being official: there is no crime here and I am the only one who has said so out loud. He is taking the light away from something. File closed for want of a complainant.

secrets.location_hint: Evidence shelf four, single catalogued box (z_evidence_room).

en.title: The Broadcast Log, and the One Caller
en.text: The station's radio room kept a log right up to the end, and the end is legible. Forty-one nights of no traffic. Then, on the forty-second, an inbound on a frequency the set should not receive: a calm voice, looping, telling whoever is listening to go to the power station and not to follow the arena signs. The duty officer logged it as a prank, logged it again as a recording, and on the third night wrote only: it answers when you talk to it. The last entry is a set of relay clicks, transcribed carefully, and beneath them a note in the same careful hand. I have started saying goodnight to it.

secrets.location_hint: Bound broadcast log on the desk in the radio room (z_radio_room), last three pages.

en.title: The Cold Room Full of Lamps
en.text: Cold storage should hold food. This one holds four hundred streetlight refractors, racked by size, wrapped individually in newspaper, at four degrees. The inventory sheet explains the cold as preservation and then, further down, as calibration — the author needed them at a constant temperature to take a reading, and he took one every night for a year. The last reading is written twice. The second is underlined and beside it, in a hand that has stopped trying to sound like a scientist: it is not remembering the light. It is remembering the people under it, and it is getting better.

secrets.location_hint: Racked shelving in cold storage (z_cold_storage), inventory sheet clipped to the door.

en.title: The Last Consignment Note
en.text: The foreman's office is tidy in the way offices get when the person tidying intends to leave and come back. On the desk, one consignment note, signed for and never filed. Destination: the center. Contents: nine refractors, one bracket assembly, and — written in the margin by the foreman, not the clerk — 'the ones from ward B, per instruction, do not open'. The note is dated night three. Whatever was moved into the center on night three came out of a hospital ward, and the man who signed for it left this on his desk where it would be found, which tells you what he thought finding it was worth.

secrets.location_hint: Unsigned-file consignment note on the foreman's desk (z_foreman_office).

en.title: Workshop B, the Night Shift He Kept
en.text: Workshop B is the only room in Factory 9 with a chair, a desk lamp and a kettle, and the shift log beside the door is not the factory's — it is one man's, kept in the same hand for nine years. He came every night after the day shift left and stayed until the hum started. The entries are measurements, then observations, then something else: the hum is not the generator. The generator is answering. On the last page, the handwriting finally shakes: I have spent nine years teaching a city to remember and I never once asked what it would do with the remembering. It is doing something with it now.

secrets.location_hint: Desk and personal shift log in workshop B (z_workshop_b), under the single desk lamp.

en.title: The Locker That Was Kept for Him
en.text: Locker 41 has a name plate and the name has been scrubbed off and written back twice, in two different hands, as if people kept needing to be sure. Inside: a lamplighter's coat, too big for anyone who works here, folded; a tin mug; and a bundle of work orders bound with wire, forty years of them, every lamp logged by hand. The crew took his records when the utility stopped keeping any, because somebody had to hold the list of what the city used to be. On the inside of the door, pencilled, a message left for a man who has not come back: we still log them. Come and read yours.

secrets.location_hint: Locker 41 in the locker room (z_locker_room); the name plate has been rewritten twice.

en.title: The Feeder He Cut Last
en.text: The switchgear room has eleven feeds and ten of them have been pulled clean — not switched, pulled, the busbars unbolted and carried away. The eleventh is intact, fused, and warm to the touch in a building with no power. Somebody has been through this room taking the grid apart with his own hands and then stopped, deliberately, with one line left live, because one line has to stay live for the thing in the center to keep drinking and he is not finished starving it. Tagged to the surviving feed with wire: LAST. DO NOT RESTORE. If you are reading this and you have come to fix the city, engineer — fix it somewhere else.

secrets.location_hint: The single surviving, still-warm feed in the switchgear room (z_switchgear_room); wire tag on the busbar.

en.title: The Boneyard, Sorted by Street
en.text: Behind the relay room the Keeper has built a graveyard, and it is organised. Four hundred and eleven lamp assemblies, stacked in rows, and every row has a hand-painted board naming a street: MAPLE ROW, HOUSE 24 BLOCK, PARK BANDSTAND, and on and on through the whole city. He did not dump them. He retired them, street by street, in the order he had lit them, and he has been walking that order backwards ever since the blackout. At the far end, one row with a board and no lamps on it yet. The board reads POWER STATION ROAD. He has saved his own street for last.

secrets.location_hint: The sorted lamp boneyard behind the relay room (z_lamp_boneyard); the empty final row is at the far end.

en.title: The Bunk That Was Still Made
en.text: The crew bunk room holds six beds and five are stripped. The sixth is made — corners folded, blanket squared, the way you make a bed you intend to come back to. On the pillow, the recorder's field book, open at the last entry, and the last entry is the one that went out on the relay: feeder four is not faulty, the draw is deliberate, we are walking the line to the substation. Below it, unfinished, in the same hand: if this is read by someone who is not us, the bench proof is at the suburbs, one streetlight, and it means the light can be kept. Marat says the center is not a place. He stopped there and did not finish the sentence and I did not ask him to.

secrets.location_hint: The sixth bunk in the crew bunk room (z_crew_bunk); the field book sits on the pillow.

en.title: The Proposal, in His Own Words
en.text: The archive holds the original Project Architect proposal, and reading it is worse than reading the denial, because it is sincere. He wanted a city that could remember. Not records — records burn. He wanted the grid itself to hold it: every lamp a witness, every lit street a memory with an address, the whole network keeping what happened on it the way a wax keeps a voice. The budget section is modest. The ethics section is one line: the city is already watching, we only propose to let it keep what it sees. He was right about the watching. He never priced the keeping, and the city has been paying for it in people ever since.

secrets.location_hint: Original proposal folder in the station archive (z_archive), shelved behind the operating manuals.

en.title: The Bunker Door, and What Is Behind It
en.text: Under the cooling yard there is a door that is not on any plan of this station, and the door has been welded shut from the outside and then unwelded from the inside, more than once, by someone with patience and a torch. Beyond it, steps going down, and on the steps, in chalk, a count. It is a count of nights, kept by somebody living down there and coming up. The most recent mark is three days old. Beside the count, a message for whoever finally follows it down: I have kept the light off it for as long as I could. It is not angry. It is patient, and it has learned every face that ever stood under a lamp on this grid. Bring your own. It will know it.

secrets.location_hint: Unplanned door under the cooling yard (z_bunker); chalk night-count on the steps beyond.

en.title: The Rig in the Signal Loft
en.text: The signal loft holds the transmitter that has been looping the call since week four, and it has not been running unattended. There is a chair, a blanket, a kettle with water in it, and a logbook with forty-one nights of the same entry: broadcast sent, no reply. Then, three weeks ago, the entry changes: reply received. Then: it is not a reply, it is an answer, and the difference matters. The last page is a conversation, written out on both sides, and the other side of it is in a hand that appears nowhere else in this building. It ends with a promise and a time. He has gone down to keep it, and he left the rig on so that you would know exactly where to come and find the end of this.

secrets.location_hint: Transmitter rig in the signal loft (z_signal_loft); the two-handed logbook lies open on the chair.
